proof_origin.place: Direct strict Roos proof using K-flat representatives

title: Closure of derived completeness under shifts
statement: Let l be a prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and X any scheme. Work in the unbounded derived category of internal modules over the continuous integral coefficient ring O_E pulled back from the profinite point to X_Proet. The canonical reduction functor at index n is derived extension to O_E/pi^(n+1). Completeness means invertibility of the specified zero-nullhomotopy Roos augmentation on a K-flat representative. For every complete object K and integer r, the shift K[r] is complete.

proof.text: Take a K-flat representative P of a complete K. A shift of P remains K-flat and represents K[r]. Its original augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism; so is its shift. The normalized signed Roos shift comparison identifies that shifted augmentation with augmentation(P[r]) followed by an isomorphism. Cancelling that isomorphism proves completeness.

lean.statement:
theorem derived_nakayama_first_reduction_shifts
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∀ K : DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X),
      IsDerivedComplete l E X K → ∀ r : ℤ,
        IsDerivedComplete l E X (K⟦r⟧)
